drivingQuestion: Why need one not be concerned that the placenta expelled by an animal bearing its firstborn came from a male offspring with firstborn sanctity?
outcomeNote: The מאי טעמא of the previous unit is settled: the offspring that would carry firstborn sanctity are a minority.

segments.he: וְכׇל הַיּוֹלְדוֹת יוֹלְדוֹת מֶחֱצָה זְכָרִים וּמֶחֱצָה נְקֵבוֹת, סְמוֹךְ מִיעוּטָא דְּנִדְמֶה לְמֶחֱצָה דִּנְקֵבוֹת, וְהָווּ לְהוּ זְכָרִים מִיעוּטָא.
segments.en: «And» furthermore, with regard to «all gestating» animals, when they «give birth, half» of their offspring are «male and half» are «female.» Therefore, one can «combine the minority» of animals that «resemble» another species «with the half» that are «females, and» arrive at the conclusion that «male» offspring that resemble their species, which are the only offspring that can be consecrated with firstborn status, «are the minority.» Accordingly, one does not need to be concerned that the placenta found was from an animal consecrated with the status of a firstborn.

moves.cueHe: וכל היולדות יולדות מחצה זכרים ומחצה נקבות
moves.summary: adds the second statistical premise — half of all offspring are female
moves.about: completing the reason the mishna permits the placenta: joining the minority of נדמה to the half that are female leaves consecrable males a minority

moves.summary: joins the two to conclude that consecrable males are a minority
